blocks.text: Mastering Excel for business development representatives on Mac

As a BDR, your spreadsheet is your command center. You need to keep track of leads, follow-ups, and meeting outcomes. Excel on Mac offers powerful tools to handle these tasks. Start by learning the core shortcuts to save time. Using the keyboard keeps your hands on the home row. You can select a full column by pressing Control + Space. Select a full row with Shift + Space. These simple moves reduce your reliance on the trackpad.

Speed matters when you have a list of one hundred prospects. Use Command + Arrow keys to jump to the end of your data ranges. If you need to fill data down a list, use Command + D. This is faster than dragging the fill handle. If you find yourself lost in a massive sheet, use the Name Box in the top left. You can assign names to ranges to jump back to your active prospect list instantly.
Organizing your outreach with conditional formatting

Visual cues help you identify who to call next. Use conditional formatting to color-code your rows. Set a rule to turn a row red if the last contact date is older than thirty days. This ensures no prospect falls through the cracks. Go to Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules. You can set specific criteria for your sales stages, such as Cold, Warm, or Demo Booked.
Managing large lead lists without errors

Data entry is often the most time-consuming part of your job. Use Data Validation to create drop-down lists for your sales stages. This prevents typos and keeps your reports clean. Go to Data > Data Validation. Select List in the Allow box. Type your stages separated by commas. This ensures every row follows the same structure, making your final exports to your CRM much smoother.
How to use Lazur with your spreadsheets

Lazur works as your assistant while you look at Excel. If you forget a shortcut, hold Option + Command and ask where to find a specific feature. Lazur will draw a circle around the menu item for you. If you are struggling with a formula, ask Lazur to explain how it works. You can also use dictation to log notes into your spreadsheet cells. Hold fn to start dictating and speak your notes directly into the cell.
Common mistakes BDRs make in Excel

items: Keeping raw data and calculated reports on the same sheet.
Hard-coding values into formulas instead of using cell references.
Failing to freeze panes when working with large datasets.
Overlooking the status bar for quick counts and averages.
Not using tables for easier sorting and filtering of lead data.

blocks.text: Tracking your follow-up schedule requires accurate dates. Use the shortcut Control + Semicolon to insert the current date into a cell. This saves you from typing the month and day manually. If you need to calculate the days since your last call, subtract the date cell from the TODAY function. This keeps your timeline dynamic.

Once you have enough data, use Pivot Tables to see your conversion rates. Select your entire dataset and choose Insert > PivotTable. Drag your sales stage to the Rows area and your lead count to the Values area. This gives you a quick snapshot of your pipeline health. You can then use a chart to present these numbers to your manager.
